title: Exercise Helps the Aging Brain Take Out the Trash
hook: Your brain has a cleaning system that flushes out waste — and it gets sluggish with age. Regular activity appears to support nearly every part of it.
key_points: The brain clears waste through its glymphatic system, which falters with age.
Researchers found exercise supports several processes that system depends on.
Those include better sleep, lower inflammation, and healthier blood vessels.
This may be part of why activity is tied to slower cognitive decline.
It's an indirect mechanism — exercise helps the cleanup, it isn't the cleanup.
content_html: Your brain generates waste, and it has a plumbing system to get rid of it: the glymphatic system, which flushes byproducts out of brain tissue. Like a lot of plumbing, it works worse with age. New research suggests regular exercise helps keep it running.
extra_html:
As ScienceDaily reports, researchers found that physical activity supports several of the processes this cleanup depends on — deeper sleep, lower inflammation, and healthier blood vessels. Each of those is a lever the glymphatic system pulls on, so exercise appears to work through them rather than acting on the brain's drainage directly.

That indirectness is worth holding onto: nobody is claiming a workout scrubs plaque out of your head. The claim is that activity keeps the conditions right for clearance to happen, and that because the system matters more the older you get, this could be one of the routes by which exercise protects against cognitive decline. It's another entry on an already long list of reasons to move — and a reminder that sleep and exercise are working the same job from two directions.

related.title: How Much Exercise You Actually Need
related.hook: The headline number is smaller than most people fear: about 150 minutes of moderate activity a week — roughly 20-some minutes a day — moves the needle on your health.

related.title: Keeping Your Brain Healthy
related.hook: No pill prevents dementia, but the habits that protect your heart turn out to protect your brain too.

related.title: Nearly Half of Dementia Risk Is Something You Can Change
related.hook: A long-term brain study tied smoking, high blood pressure, heart disease, and high blood lipids to the damage behind vascular dementia — risks that are all treatable.

flashcards.back_html: The brain's waste-clearance system — it flushes out harmful byproducts. It becomes less efficient with age, which is why its upkeep matters more as we get older.

flashcards.prompt: How does exercise appear to help the brain's waste-clearance system?

choices.text: Indirectly — by improving sleep, lowering inflammation, and keeping blood vessels healthy
By directly pumping waste out of the skull during a workout
By replacing the system entirely with a different clearance route

flashcards.explanation_html: Researchers found activity supports several processes the glymphatic system relies on: sleep quality, inflammation levels, and vascular health.

flashcards.prompt: Why does waste clearance matter more as you age?

choices.text: The system grows less efficient, so buildup is linked to cognitive decline
The brain produces no waste until old age

flashcards.explanation_html: The cleanup system becomes increasingly important — and increasingly strained — with age, which is why supporting it could help protect against cognitive decline.
